quests.sentence: She completes the assignment carefully.
quests.hint: Manner adverbs like carefully usually go at the end of the sentence, after the object.
quests.explanation: Carefully describes how she completes the assignment, so it follows the object assignment at the end of the sentence — the typical position for manner adverbs.

quests.sentence: He explains the instructions clearly.
quests.hint: The word describing how he explains comes after the thing being explained.
quests.explanation: Clearly modifies the verb explains and sits after the object instructions, confirming that manner adverbs typically follow the object rather than the verb directly.

quests.sentence: The mechanic repairs the engine skillfully.
quests.hint: Even with a different subject and object, the manner word still finishes the sentence.
quests.explanation: Skillfully describes the manner of the repair and stays at the very end, after the object engine, matching the pattern from the previous two sentences.

quests.sentence: She usually finishes her work.
quests.hint: Frequency words like usually go in the middle, right before the main verb.
quests.explanation: Usually sits between the subject She and the main verb finishes — this middle position is standard for frequency adverbs with an ordinary verb.

quests.sentence: They often discuss new ideas.
quests.hint: Often takes the same middle spot: after the subject, before the verb.
quests.explanation: Often goes directly after the subject They and before the verb discuss, following the same mid-position rule as usually.

quests.sentence: Our team rarely misses a deadline.
quests.hint: A multi-word subject doesn't change anything — the frequency word still sits right before the verb.
quests.explanation: Rarely comes after the full subject Our team and before misses, showing that mid-position holds even when the subject itself has two words.

quests.sentence: He is always punctual.
quests.hint: With is/am/are, the frequency word moves after the verb, not before it.
quests.explanation: Unlike ordinary verbs, is places the frequency adverb always right after itself: He is always punctual, not He always is punctual.

quests.sentence: The weather is often unpredictable.
quests.hint: The same rule applies here: the frequency word follows is, not the subject directly.
quests.explanation: Often comes immediately after is, following the rule that frequency adverbs sit right after forms of be rather than before them.

quests.sentence: Customers are sometimes impatient.
quests.hint: Sometimes slots in right after are, just like always and often did after is.
quests.explanation: Are pairs with sometimes directly after it, confirming that all forms of be — is, are, was, were — place the frequency word right after them.

quests.sentence: She checks her email in the morning.
quests.hint: A time expression like in the morning usually comes at the very end of the sentence.
quests.explanation: In the morning tells us when she checks her email, and time expressions typically close the sentence, after the verb and object.

quests.sentence: We clean the office on weekends.
quests.hint: On weekends works the same way — it answers 'when' and goes last.
quests.explanation: On weekends is a time expression that comes after the object the office, showing when the cleaning happens, at the end of the sentence.

quests.sentence: The store closes at midnight.
quests.hint: Even a single word like midnight, paired with at, still closes the sentence as a time phrase.
quests.explanation: At midnight functions as one time expression and sits at the end, right after the verb closes, with no object needed here.

quests.sentence: He works at the hospital.
quests.hint: A place expression like at the hospital tells us where and comes at the end.
quests.explanation: At the hospital answers 'where' and follows the verb works at the end of the sentence, since there is no object to separate them from.

quests.sentence: They study in the library.
quests.hint: In the library also answers 'where' and takes the same end position after the verb.
quests.explanation: In the library follows study directly, showing that place expressions consistently come after the verb when there's no object.

quests.sentence: The children play in the park.
quests.hint: A plural subject doesn't change the rule — the place phrase still ends the sentence.
quests.explanation: In the park comes after play to show where the children are playing, keeping the place expression in its usual end position.

quests.sentence: She exercises at the gym every evening.
quests.hint: When place and time appear together, place comes first and time comes second, both at the end.
quests.explanation: At the gym (place) comes before every evening (time); English orders multiple end-of-sentence expressions as place before time.

quests.sentence: He meets clients at the showroom every Tuesday.
quests.hint: The object comes right after the verb, then place, then time — in that fixed order.
quests.explanation: Clients (object) follows meets, then at the showroom (place) comes next, and every Tuesday (time) comes last, following object-place-time order.

quests.sentence: We volunteer at the shelter every weekend.
quests.hint: Place still comes before time even without an object in the sentence.
quests.explanation: At the shelter (place) precedes every weekend (time), confirming the place-before-time rule holds whether or not there's a direct object.

quests.sentence: She sings beautifully in the shower.
quests.hint: When manner and place both appear, manner comes first, then place, both after the verb.
quests.explanation: Beautifully (manner) comes right after sings, and in the shower (place) follows it — manner is placed closer to the verb than place.

quests.sentence: He drives carefully through the city.
quests.hint: The same manner-then-place order applies: how he drives, then where he drives.
quests.explanation: Carefully (manner) precedes through the city (place), matching the pattern of manner coming before place after the verb drives.

quests.sentence: The children play happily in the garden.
quests.hint: A plural subject doesn't disturb the order — manner still leads, place still follows.
quests.explanation: Happily (manner) comes directly after play, and in the garden (place) comes after that, keeping the manner-before-place sequence intact.

quests.sentence: She always speaks confidently.
quests.hint: Frequency still sits in the middle before the verb, while manner still closes the sentence.
quests.explanation: Always (frequency) sits between She and speaks in mid-position, while confidently (manner) closes the sentence — the two adverb types keep their separate usual spots.

quests.sentence: He often responds quickly.
quests.hint: The same split applies: frequency word before the verb, manner word after it.
quests.explanation: Often stays in its mid-position before responds, and quickly stays at the end, showing frequency and manner adverbs don't compete for the same slot.

quests.sentence: Our manager usually explains things clearly.
quests.hint: A longer subject and object don't change where each adverb type goes.
quests.explanation: Usually sits in mid-position right before explains, and clearly closes the sentence after the object things, confirming both rules hold together in one sentence.

quests.sentence: She works quietly in the workshop every afternoon.
quests.hint: Chain the end-of-sentence details in order: how, then where, then when.
quests.explanation: Quietly (manner), in the workshop (place), and every afternoon (time) follow that exact order after the verb works — manner, then place, then time.

quests.sentence: He negotiates calmly in the boardroom every Friday.
quests.hint: The object comes first, then manner, then place, then time, all trailing the verb in sequence.
quests.explanation: Calmly (manner) follows negotiates, then in the boardroom (place), then every Friday (time) — the manner-place-time chain stays fixed regardless of context.

quests.sentence: They rehearse patiently at the theater every Monday evening.
quests.hint: Even with a longer time phrase, the manner-place-time order at the end doesn't change.
quests.explanation: Patiently (manner), at the theater (place), and every Monday evening (time) line up in that order, showing the chain still works with a two-word time expression.

quests.sentence: The nurses always check patients carefully in the ward.
quests.hint: Combine what you know: frequency goes mid-sentence, then object, then manner, then place at the end.
quests.explanation: Always sits in mid-position before check, patients is the object, carefully (manner) follows it, and in the ward (place) closes the sentence — three adverbial rules working together.

quests.sentence: Our team always communicates clearly during important meetings.
quests.hint: Frequency stays mid-sentence, manner follows the verb, and a time-like expression closes the sentence.
quests.explanation: Always (frequency) precedes communicates, clearly (manner) follows it, and during important meetings (a time-like expression) ends the sentence, reviewing several adverb rules at once.

quests.sentence: She practices diligently at the studio every Saturday morning.
quests.hint: Manner comes right after the verb, then place, then time — the full chain from earlier in this file.
quests.explanation: Diligently (manner), at the studio (place), and every Saturday morning (time) follow the verb practices in the established manner-place-time order, closing out this file's adverb skills.
